To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) learned descriptors outperform SIFT on a standard benchmark for image retrieval, and (2) learned descriptors out-perform SIFT in the presence of cluttered backgrounds.

(a) the learned descriptors outperform SIFT in terms of recognition performance, (b) the learned descriptors show a higher distinctiveness, i.e. a higher number of distinct descriptors, and (c) the learned descriptors are more robust against changes in viewpoint and illumination.

(1) the proposed trainable models are able to learn descriptors that are more robust than SIFT descriptors; and (2) the proposed models are able to outperform SIFT descriptors in the task of matching keypoints in images.
